occurrences across 16 llama.cpp and ggml libraries. The paths came from
the fetched source tree. The Android NDK CMake build now uses Clang file
prefix mapping for the source and build directories. Native messages
retain relative filenames.
[Compiler option reference](https://clang.llvm.org/docs/ClangCommandLineReference.html#cmdoption-clang-ffile-prefix-map).

The rebuilt debug and unsigned release APKs each contain the original
32 native members across four ABIs and zero matches for the workstation
path markers. Both inference ABIs still contain relative source names.
NDK llvm-readelf verified the same library names, dependencies, and
dynamic symbol contracts across all 32 release members. Twelve release
members were byte-identical. All 1,243 JVM cases and both lint variants
passed. The first offline LFM3 smoke preflight timed out hashing the
existing model before installing either debug package. That runtime
check remains pending.

On the earlier 73f68da hosted run, Android 8 shard 0 passed 595 methods.

## Compact phone composer and standard device reconciliation

The phone composer keeps Chat options beside the draft, outside the
weighted transcript and optional controls. The compact header responds to
the editor focus and IME inset. The regression waits for a focused visible
editor and native IME, verifies the edit reached the composer, then checks
the same unsent draft after closing the helper. It checks zero sends and
zero helper model requests.

The revised snapshot passed 1,242 JVM cases and both lint variants. The
debug and instrumentation pair passed eight focused cases per API on
Android 8 and 17. Both emulators also passed the focused draft regression
at 840 × 1470 pixels, 420 dpi and 1.3× font scale and restored the original
display settings. The main emulator packages retained their installed APK
digests. The earlier compact logs preserve the preceding menu visibility
and original-draft failures. The revised Android 17 compact attempt lost
window focus while an older production app had an Android “Application Not
Responding” dialog. After stopping that emulator process, the same debug
APK pair passed the compact test. Both the failed and passing logs remain
in private evidence.

The separate a6e3704 candidate passed the complete standard device
inventory with 1,261 Android 8 cases from hosted CI and 1,262 Android 17
cases from the owned emulator using the byte-identical hosted APK pair.
The Android 17 rerun passed 595 and 667 cases in its two shards. The
original hosted run retains the compact helper and workspace review
failures. Physical-model cases require separate acceptance.
[Hosted run and its original result](https://github.com/DionCroft/Signal_Grove/actions/runs/45386612152).

The revised composer requires a full matrix on the final release source.
The signed Xiaomi upgrade, production retention and public updater checks
remain open.

## Hermes Activity approval and answer waits

The Activity panel now uses the existing authenticated control records for the
selected conversation and run. It filters foreign, stale-generation, resolved
and unidentified requests, and omits live waits for read-only history.
The summary shows approval or answer status, response state and the original
local receipt time. The existing decision dialog handles prompts, choices and
submission. The same source passed 1,243 JVM tests in 118 reports, debug and
release lint with zero errors, and both debug APK assemblies.

The signed debug pair passed ten focused native cases on Android 8 and 17.
These cover the new Demo approval wait, its settled removal and prompt privacy,
plus existing approvals, clarification, Activity telemetry, migration and
profile/history cases. The exact new approval case passed on both emulators
at 840 × 1470, 420 dpi and 1.3× text. Screen settings and installed production
APK digests verified after the runs. Live Hermes and the separate beta.11
production gates still need their own evidence.

## Runs Activity payload privacy

Hermes v0.23.4 can populate the Runs stream preview from tool progress
and serialized results. The prior beta.11 candidate stored that preview
and displayed it as selectable timeline text. The static wire scope
also accepted free-form subagent goals, output and file lists. The new
decoder retains tool identities, timings, reported outcomes, subagent
lineage and accounting. Legacy rows use the same display boundary.
[Upstream preview producer](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/8fc0374447313e276f6b9a2764bfc750190c966a/gateway/platforms/api_server_runs.py#L136-L158).

The method fixtures send distinct synthetic raw tool and delegated
payloads, then inject a saved legacy row containing both a preview
and summary. The UI verifies the legacy call is displayed without its
payload. The live timeline retains separate parallel calls and the
requested and served runtime identities. The suite also covers
unavailable read-only history, profile switching, migration and
receipt ownership.

The verified debug pair passed all seven selected methods on Android 8
and 17. Both owned production package digests matched their preflight
values. The JVM suite passed 1,242 cases across 118 reports. Debug
lint reported 56 warnings and release lint 55, with zero errors in
either. The exact release-source matrix and final candidate signing
are separate gates.

both Android 8 and Android 17. The selected methods cover parallel
tool and child activity, served model reporting, stale identity
isolation, read-only history, SQLite migration, reconnect without

restored their original keyboard preferences and preserved their
installed production APKs during the fixture runs. Two selector

each method's class from the verified instrumentation source.

unobscured editor saved the exact revised test title before the

and public updater acceptance remain open.

qualifiers at 3.43.0 after the Guava update. The first strict isolated
resolution stopped at missing checker and JUnit checksums. The new
constraint retained the prior qualifier selection and the two JUnit

## Hermes client stamp retry compatibility

The three changed modules in the reviewed main persistence layout
normalize only the owner-stamped client label for input retry identity.
The original payload written to a new queued admission still carries
the label. [First stamped writer](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/commit/0357a14b76e4f604d2fa6b9c3a973f9a76f7968d) ·
[Normalization change](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/commit/6dae08d3b8b8c2d56e93553175502e318036d783).

The isolated probe used the original SQLite modules and three disposable
profile stores. Each Python source matched the official complete Git
tree for its exact revision. The candidate ran on Windows CPython 3.14.3
with the locked YAML wheels. Hermes selected the DELETE journal fallback
for the installed SQLite 3.50.4. The 239 imported candidate files were
byte-identical at `a15b971` and `eb49b89`. The executable check ran
at `a15b971`.

| Stored input | Queued and retired readback after upgrade |
| --- | --- |
| Written at `242315c` before the stamp existed | The same request recovered the original receipt with a new stamp or without one. |
| Written at `0357a14` with a stamp included in the old digest | The original admission IDs and receipts survived. Identical, changed and absent stamp retries each returned `admission_conflict`. |
| Written at `a15b971` with normalized retry identity | A changed or absent stamp recovered the original receipt. The queued record preserved its first stamp. Changes to text, intent or other surface fields were refused in the exercised paths. |

The candidate verified unchanged admission and receipt tables across
the retry checks, SQLite integrity and foreign keys, and one claim for
the fresh input. A retired request from a different principal was
refused. This establishes a persistence result for the exercised
inputs. The exact gateway's receipt authority was then exercised on
a byte-identical copy of the synthetic stamped store. Two reads by
the same fixture actor returned the original queued receipt. A different
principal, different profile, missing submit capability and mismatched
session each produced the expected refusal. The native route gave
not-found for the deleted session while SQLite still returned its
original completed receipt. The active admission row and retained
receipt matched before and after the reads. No admission or execution
was retried.

The fixture called the native handler with constructed actors and one
dormant session. Transport authentication and production upgrade
acceptance remain open. The first input check used the wrong cached
Git tree schema. A second probe mistook two logical receipts for two
current rows. Independent read-only reconciliation found one identical
active row in both copies, and the corrected probe checked the active
row and retained receipt separately. The strict compatibility gate
remains in force.

## Focused Android keyboard and helper consent checks

The original [hosted matrix](https://github.com/DionCroft/Signal_Grove/actions/runs/45287698016)
passed both Android 17 shards and Android 8 shard 0. Android 8 shard 1
failed four methods. The first local correction passed eight of nine
checks on each API. Android 8 stopped before the helper's first tap.
Android 17 passed fresh helper consent and failed the document control's
position check while the keyboard was visible. Both intermediate logs
are retained alongside the original hosted evidence.

The corrected tests choose a visible portion of each helper control and
send one guarded Android tap per action. They still require fresh consent
when the observations change. The document test waits for a complete
Review sources button above the real keyboard before performing one tap.
The other checks observe actual app window focus and native IME visibility
and retain their existing consent, clipboard and draft assertions.

The sealed debug build passed all 1,242 JVM tests across 118 suites and
debug lint reported 56 warnings and zero errors. Both API 26 and API 37
passed all nine named methods. Each reported two successful consent taps
and two successful Run taps, with one accepted DOWN and UP per tap.
The runner checked the existing debug signer and each installed artifact,
restored both emulator keyboard settings and verified the production APK
digests on both devices. These are focused emulator checks.

## Beta.11 inventory and Android 8 shard failures

The exact signed rehearsal produces a [CycloneDX 1.6](https://cyclonedx.org/schema/bom-1.6.schema.json)
inventory with 187 components. The sealed source was verified before and
after a successful offline release runtime resolution. It records 154
Maven modules and 99 binary artifact observations, including one exact
duplicate androidx.core AAR record. The 98 distinct file hashes all
match Gradle's pinned verification metadata. Maven coordinates and
artifact hashes agree with the released beta.10 inventory.

All 32 native libraries were hashed from the signed APK. Their ELF
architectures matched the four ABI directories, and the packaged native
dependencies were checked against their actual ELF imports. The APK paths
agree with beta.10, while 20 native file hashes differ. Provenance binds
the SBOM, exact build and source receipts, signing certificate, native
upstream pin and verified API 26 upgrade. Generated artifacts remain on
E: and are scoped to this rehearsal.

Android 8 shard 0 passed in the [hosted matrix](https://github.com/DionCroft/Signal_Grove/actions/runs/45287698016).
Shard 1 started all 667 methods and had 663 distinct positive results.
The four failures were:

- Fresh helper consent left its checkbox off after selecting it.
- The copied long reply test did not observe the activity resize for its keyboard.
- The temporary chat observed no focused dialog during the IME transition.
- The plugin settings test observed no focused window while closing the keyboard.

On the locally verified debug pair, three of those methods passed. The
helper test failed after the observation changed because the unshared
request was never dispatched. This differs from the hosted checkbox
failure and preserves the need to verify both interactions under load.
The failed hosted artifact and focused local log remain separate.

protected account state. The prior publication catalog pointed under
the Hermes project home. The renderer now supplies a single fixed policy
destination derived from the account home, and the catalog consumes it.
The deployment review packet changes only the policy path and its
observed ancestors. The exact two wrappers and two systemd overrides
retain their previously checked bytes.

matched the original observation. The fresh observation bounded the
subsequent owned test.

published at the corrected path and rolled the policy and runtime

loaded exactly the four reviewed workspace handlers. The original and
restored registry both had zero Signal Grove methods.

dispatch, network calls or job replay.

## Windows branch reference hold

A disposable fixture previously advanced a branch while the native guard
held HEAD open. The admission path now keeps Git's verify-only transaction
prepared for the exact reviewed commit, alongside the existing Windows
handles for the root, Git metadata and HEAD. Git aborts the transaction on
pipe closure and releases the ref lock. This is a temporary Git metadata
operation in the authorized admission path. Checkout observation remains
read-only. Git's checkout hooks are disabled for the guard.
[Git reference transaction semantics](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-update-ref).

Native Windows fixtures passed **86 cases**, including **14 checkout
cases**, with zero failures, errors or skips and matching source hashes.
The six new cases prove that Git cannot advance loose or packed refs while
the guard holds them, and can advance them again after admission fails.
They also cover drift before transaction preparation, a symbolic branch
at the same commit, a redirected Git common directory, and hook exclusion.
Receipt SHA-256: `2e9209515aaad0aaecf8b5df2ed6b1e8216bd6d86a39d0b6175d368fc686ae49`.

The covered boundary is a local context for cooperating Git writers.

## Exact reviewed Windows checkout

The optional worker checkout check uses the existing enrolled
`WorkspaceProvider` for the protected scope, current registered root and
worker instance. Its snapshot includes the full native directory IDs of the
root and Git metadata plus the branch, commit and registration revision.
Before an admission, it rereads the binding and checks that snapshot. The
owner's registered path and Git HEAD remain open with native no-delete
sharing. The HEAD handle also refuses a concurrent writer. The check itself
is read-only and supplies no write grant, approval or job identity.

Git uses fixed, local plumbing commands and the operator-selected native
binary. Inherited Git environment redirection is excluded, as are optional
locks, replacements and lazy fetching. The worktree reported by Git must
match the registered root. Linked metadata and detached HEAD are refused at
this boundary. This is an admission-time check. Subsequent mutations and the
native launch still need their own scoped enforcement.
[Git command options](https://git-scm.com/docs/git) · [Revision resolution](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-rev-parse).

Eight Windows cases use disposable checkouts and the real Git executable.
A concurrent HEAD replacement was refused while the guard held it.

replaced folder at the same path, new worker instance, retired worker,
registry drift and checkout redirection. The existing test runner recorded
80 native passes with zero failures or skips and no source changes.
The 130 portable workspace cases passed. The full portable suite discovered
1,228 tests with zero failures and 273 platform or fixture skips. Native result
JSON SHA-256 `0bc5bb07dca73b2e8c385dd1bff85d33940e3957b59da4891615f692009a669b`.

## Android scheduled project approval inbox

In **Hermes management → Scheduled jobs → Project approvals**, an
authenticated owner can review the exact held occurrence, original due time,
project and workspace, branch, worker, task and write access. The app uses the
same owner transport through prepare and decision. Leaving the screen, changing
profile or reaching the review deadline closes that transport.

Before Approve or Deny, Room saves the original occurrence and its due time
with the authenticated identity and verified home. The receipt excludes the
task and workspace text. Defer closes the review while leaving the original
occurrence held. After a lost decision response, a new authenticated transport
can observe the exact occurrence. An unknown or missing retained result stays
unresolved. A verified compact terminal decision can settle the receipt after
the native execution detail is pruned. Generic receipt clearing cannot settle
these pending decisions.

Two rendered Android fixture cases exercised Approve with a lost reply and
unknown-to-completed recovery, and Defer followed by a fresh Deny review.
The fixtures checked that the receipt existed before either durable decision
arrived, that no duplicate approval was sent, and that the two settlement
paths used the original occurrence. Protocol tests cover exact receipt and
execution identity and reject a mismatched profile, time or occurrence.

## Decisions for exact scheduled project occurrences

The protected owner route binds a review to one occurrence, live actor
and transport, catalogue and policy generations, and the resolved
project, workspace, branch, worker, task and access. The approval
rechecks these values under the native job and fire locks. An approval
or denial reserves a compact decision and native execution in one
SQLite transaction. The job and due instant also have a unique key.
Native terminal outcomes are copied to the compact decision before
ordinary execution pruning. Original receipt reads use the protected
profile database and can return the decision when execution detail has
expired. Defer closes the review and leaves the occurrence held.
[Protocol and settlement rules](../server_extensions/coordinator_workspaces/README.md#decide-one-held-project-occurrence).

through strict native owner dispatch and one fresh-process case:

- Absent operator setup, another profile and a foreign transport refused.
  Deferral retained the exact job with no native execution row.
- A changed worker instance and an expired review could not reserve.
- Denial wrote a cancelled receipt without starting work. A recurring job
  advanced, a one-shot paused and both retained their unused repeat budget.
- Closing the original transport just after saving the fire claim left
  a single task callback and the same completed occurrence on reconnect.
- Competing reviews on two owner transports reserved one exact attempt.
- Pruning the terminal native row kept the compact completed decision.
  A second execution ID for that job and instant was refused.
- A catalogue save failure after reservation retained the claim receipt
  with zero dispatches for that occurrence. It refused both replay and a
  second review.
- A lost worker response recorded unknown for the original execution and
  kept its fire claim for reconciliation.
- A fresh process marked the interrupted attempt unknown through the
  native recovery function. Pruning retained the compact unknown result,
  and the native ticker left the job held.

read-only catalogue and receipt adapter. The native job locks, SQLite

## Android reviewed Run once and original receipt

Scheduled job details open a foreground review on a separate canonical
owner connection. The review displays the signed-in identity, task,
read or write access, exact workspace and worker, and the project and branch
when present. Approve, Defer and Deny reuse that connection. Closing the
review, leaving the management screen or reaching its deadline closes the
connection. The optional operator contract returns an explanation when
reviewed Run once is unavailable.

Room stores the original request and its owner, profile, job and verified
home before confirmation. Task and scope text stay out of the receipt.
A claimed or running attempt stays unresolved. A lost confirmation uses a
separate authenticated observation to read the original execution. A verified
terminal result settles the same receipt. A foreign connection, actor or
home sees only pending metadata. Generic review cannot clear the pending run.

## Native pause-preserving Run once

Staging with both reviewed native hashes enables an internal manual claim
and settlement hook. The hook checks the job and execution stores share the
same profile. It holds the per-job fire fence and strict jobs lock while
its caller checks approval against a copy of the exact stored job. The
native ledger reserves the original ID before the job claim is saved.
Settlement records the manual outcome while preserving pause, repeat,
the scheduled instant and automatic retry state. A normal tick leaves
that occurrence available while the reviewed manual fire is live.
[Staging and call boundary](../server_extensions/coordinator_workspaces/README.md#optional-native-run-once-receipts).

The Git-verified v0.23.1 and main `242315c` modules each passed six isolated cases:

- A denied approval and a mixed job or ledger profile produce no original attempt.
- An exact claim requires both native locks and refuses a busy job or stale completion.
- The native in-process scheduler saved a fixture result and completed its original
  ledger row while leaving a finite one-shot paused with its repeat budget intact.
- An active due occurrence stayed untouched during the live manual claim and
  became eligible after settlement. A failed manual run preserved its schedule,
  quota and retry settings.
- An injected job-store write failure left one original claimed row. A second
  reservation of that ID failed, with the saved job unchanged.

The scheduler fixture substitutes a deterministic task result and uses the
native in-process delivery and bookkeeping path. The next gates include
exact approval consumption, detached worker execution and recovery, and a

import order problem in the test harness. A stale stock function advanced
the fixture one-shot. The corrected harness imports the staged jobs and
ledger before the scheduler and asserts its bound callables.

## Strict paused schedule editing source

The optional native adapter supports owner-scoped prepare, apply
and receipt observation for timing edits to a paused, unclaimed job.
The review version binds the bytes and identity of the protected
catalogue. Apply requires the cross-process native lock and
rechecks the selected ID and review before the native writer saves
anything. Stock calls retain their existing lock behavior.
The timing and original request receipt are written together in
the same native catalogue replacement. A same-request replay with
identical fields reads the retained receipt. A conflicting reuse
or stale review refuses. A lost post-save readback is marked as
possibly submitted and can be observed by the original ID.

## Unbound work during the original gateway drain window

before accepting a gateway idle response during drain. The owner, incremented
epoch and unbound count come from one query-only read transaction against the
existing ledger. A positive count is recorded and the actor keeps sampling
within the original five-second window. An invalid, foreign or missing
snapshot holds the operation. The actor still reads the complete ledger
before recording a successful drain. The observer never acquires a SQLite
writer transaction.

An isolated Windows component trial used real maintained SDK turn scopes,
receipts, freeze methods and the original unbound-blind status observer. It
used an in-process adapter for the live-work portion of the status payload
and for transport. The settled case observed zero twice in the old status
and one then zero directly. The original turn finished while frozen, and the
window settled in 0.218 seconds. In the held case the old observer reported
zero 25 times while the direct count stayed one. The window held at 5.001
seconds. The fixture then finished its original turn and retained the frozen
fence. Independent readback found one finished unbound receipt, one freeze,
zero registered turns and SQLite integrity `ok` in each case.

## Attached workspace and Windows worker read checkpoint

On Windows, the source-pinned Hermes v0.23.1 authority created and resumed a
disposable chat, moved it to a registered fixture workspace using the expected
revision and execution generation, and read the new workspace back through
`session.info`. The coordinator's operator adapter then described the worker
and used its actual Windows named pipe to prepare that root, list `note.txt`
and preview all 26 bytes. The root matched Hermes' workspace, and the returned
length, text and SHA-256 matched the fixture. The worker observed the actual
interactive Windows process identity. The chat row, observer subscription and
fixture files remained intact after the reads. No message, task admission or
worker execution record was created.

The test also refused a missing operator capability, an ungranted project, a
mismatched worker instance, an invalid binding token and an invalid file token.
All 13 combined checks passed, along with 18 original native coordinator
checks, 119 portable workspace tests and 72 Windows-native tests. This change
adds a validation probe and evidence. The hosted protocol, Windows-native and
coordinator POSIX checks also passed on the initial verification commit.
[Hosted run](https://github.com/DionCroft/Signal_Grove/actions/runs/44856192657).

The fixture also tried a directory absent from the Hermes host. The native
workspace operation returned `invalid_params`. The session row was unchanged,
the directory stayed absent and the worker received no call. The upstream
workspace mutation resolves and checks the directory on the authority host.
[Hermes v0.23.1 workspace implementation](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/3b421578588243f920886e6fe79a6faa87ea026e/gateway/session_mutation_policy.py#L37-L55).

Reproduce with `scripts/probe_workspace_coordinator.py --windows-attached-worker
--source-root <clean-Hermes-v0.23.1-checkout> --work-root <new-E-drive-directory>`
using the pinned Hermes dependencies and an active Windows interactive session.
The probe checks upstream commit
`3b421578588243f920886e6fe79a6faa87ea026e`, applies the adapter in memory and
keeps the SQLite database, protected registration fixture and report in that
directory. It injects a trusted owner identity, skips incidental Git metadata
and model discovery, and calls the worker RPC directly on the same host.
It leaves deployed services, credentials and workstation project files untouched.

The combined test compares the authoritative session cwd with the prepared
Windows root. The v1 workspace methods still scope reads by owner, profile,
worker and project independently of the conversation attachment. Production
needs an explicit server-owned association between the authenticated session,
the enrolled worker project and its registered root. That association must work
even when Hermes has a different local cwd. Bind reads to the current session
revision and execution generation, and discard replies if the attachment or
registration changes during a read. Authenticated Android-to-Pi-to-worker
acceptance remains open.

## Hermes-reported context and compression

The followed session can read the effective and configured windows, current
context, last prompt size and compression count with **Read Hermes context**.
The request uses only the attached session ID on a fresh profile-bound socket.

## LFM3 context capacity probe on the Xiaomi

One in-place debug APK pair measured the pinned QAD Q4_0 LFM3 model with
four CPU threads at 4,096, 8,192 and 16,384 context tokens. All three runs
used the same 64-token short prompt and a 384-token output reserve. The
near-window workload used the measured tokenizer count and the same
reserve. Android had Wi-Fi enabled and mobile data disabled throughout.
The debug package, companion and production package kept their UIDs.

| Window | Load | Short prompt first text | Near-window input | Near-window result | Stop | Peak sampled PSS |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- | ---: | ---: |
| 4,096 | 979 ms | 3.047 s | 3,712 tokens | First text 56.800 s, completed in 57.606 s | 11 ms | 2,323,216 KiB |
| 8,192 | 954 ms | 3.145 s | 7,808 tokens | Generation deadline at 180 s | 16 ms | 2,427,176 KiB |
| 16,384 | 898 ms | 3.209 s | 16,000 tokens | Generation deadline at 180 s | 27 ms | 2,610,634 KiB |

Each run refused a one-token overflow without streaming output and
returned CANCELLED on an explicit Stop during the near-window request.
Android reported thermal status 0 throughout the samples. The two
timed-out runs did not report near-window first-text timings. These are
individual synthetic trials, with sustained thermal and battery behavior
still open. The production load route enforces 4,096 tokens.

On the same phone and APK pair, the separate 512-token boundary check
refused 489 input tokens plus a 24-token reserve and generated with a
23-token reserve. It passed in 8.187 s. On the Android 17 x86_64 emulator
with networking off, the staged repeat completed load and overflow
refusal, then reached the 120-second deadline during exact-fit generation.
The original ambiguous failure and the staged result remain recorded.
The emulator radio settings and default network were restored.

The frozen app and companion SHA-256 values were
9837a72fa38d18620a73c79d38eac178dcb7a76621da54fd2baacfda118d9d94 and 2d4ce29e1aef5eda2ed7069dd3943c1f81f739b7395859ed23958f263a2f2bac.
The exact app sources passed 1,204 JVM checks, both lint variants and
debug, test and release assembly. The packaged native symbol tables
export the probe only on ARM64 and x86_64 debug. All four release ABIs
expose only standard load. The external-model inventory now lists 15
explicit methods, including one debug probe with three separate capacity
arguments. Its 65 policy and standard-matrix accounting checks passed.

## Phone model library durability

The model store syncs Android directory entries before acknowledging the
published model, performance settings or model deletion. It also uses
the shared durable creation path for new private directories. Explicit
repeat requests verify an already published model and sync the directory
before reporting success. Import and settings failures refresh the
observed library while keeping the operation error visible.

Two JVM regressions check directory creation and the publication order.
They inject a sync failure after the file operation and verify that it
cannot return success. The visible bytes survive for reconciliation by
an explicit retry. This build passed 1,202 JVM tests across
113 reports, with zero lint errors in debug and release.

Both owned Android emulators passed real LFM3 cancellation after import
publication, plus Qwen import, generation, history read and deletion.
The Android 17 guest also passed switching between the verified Qwen
and LFM3 files with chat bindings preserved. Both guests had no default
network at test admission. The native APKs, package UIDs, original app
files and staged inputs were verified, and the previous network
settings were restored. These checks cover the filesystem calls and
lifecycle on this build. The normal Android 8 reboot evidence is
[recorded above](#offline-qwen-history-after-a-normal-android-8-reboot).
Physical and production acceptance remain open.

The first Android 8 radio command was refused before any test. A
verified Settings switch then supplied the offline condition. The
first Android 17 import completed while its host parser rejected the
extra diagnostic fields. Its terminal log was checked without
repeating the case. Both initial attempts remain in the evidence.

temporary chat continues to discard its content independently of the saved
draft. Project cancellation stays in the dialog footer while a request is
running, including while the project list is scrolled.

remained unknown with exactly one admission in the fixture. The Phone
startup setup test passed locally on both APIs.

and persistence, and sharing redacted observations resets after each
request and on topic changes.

## Offline voice in phone chat

Phone voice reuses Android speech services. Dictation selects Android's
on-device recognizer, requests the installed-language inventory before
listening, and uses only a returned compatible language. Android 13 or
later is required for the language check. An older Android version, a
missing service, or an unverified language has an explanation in the
screen. The editor can put the reviewed transcript into the current
phone draft. That action preserves the existing draft, checks the exact
chat and UTF-8 limit, and leaves Send as a separate action.

Read aloud chooses an installed voice whose Android descriptor reports
no network requirement. It verifies the applied voice before speaking.
Stop and leaving release playback and audio focus. Focus loss and the
Android audio route warning stop playback, which requires a fresh
tap to start again. Leaving discards any unapplied transcript.
[Android installed recognition languages](https://developer.android.com/reference/android/speech/RecognitionSupport#getInstalledOnDeviceLanguages()) ·
[Android voice network flag](https://developer.android.com/reference/android/speech/tts/Voice#isNetworkConnectionRequired()).

The strict build passed 1,196 JVM tests and both lint variants with zero
errors. The Android 8 and 17 emulators each passed 152 focused methods,
including the existing voice controls, per-draft opt-in and lifecycle.
The real app preserved draft text and exposed no network speech switches
while the Hermes voice preferences allowed network speech. Controller
tests verified compatible language selection, exact local reply binding,
and draft bounds. Android 17 played the synthetic reply through an installed voice with
networking off. Android reported an active speech player, and audio
focus was released on Stop and when leaving the app. All 8 pre-existing
model and chat files kept their hashes and the emulator network
settings were restored. Early harness attempts exposed raw-transfer
verification and a focus-dump spacing error. The captured audio state
and the corrected run are retained on the test host.

## Separate protected personal-profile backups

From Personal profiles, choose the complete profiles to export. The
selection starts empty, and the passphrase is entered twice before
preparing the file. Profile backups use the separate `.sgprofiles`
format. They contain the selected profile names, preferences and notes.
Android's document picker lets the user choose the file location.

The format authenticates a bounded payload with the existing backup
cryptography and a separate format identifier. Restore inspects the
entire file before showing its contents. Identical profiles are flagged
as already present. A conflicting ID can be restored as a separate copy.
The user selects the entries to add and confirms the restore. The
preference transaction checks the reviewed library again before
adding all selected profiles together. Unlocked profiles and passphrase
input have no disk staging in the backup flow.

The strict build passed 1,193 JVM tests and both lint variants with zero
errors. Android 8 and Android 17 each passed all 140 selected methods.
Tests covered encrypted selection, wrong passphrases, tampering,
size bounds, wrong archive type, stale review, capacity, and conflict
copies. Android's content-provider fixture restored one reviewed copy
and verified original chat and profile data.

A normal-app Android 17 trial used the actual document picker with
networking disabled. The app saved a protected file of
306 bytes, authenticated it at restore, and put
the reviewed note back into Personal profiles. All
8 existing model and chat files kept their
hashes, and the test restored the original network settings. The test
driver first missed the picker's uppercase SAVE control. It continued
from the pending picker and verified the one resulting file.

## Personal profiles with a reviewed phone-model request

Personal profiles store up to eight named collections of manually
entered preferences and notes. The user may edit or delete them.
Creating a profile leaves ordinary Chat Send unchanged. To use a
profile, the user selects items for an individual draft and reviews
the exact message and chosen context. Selection starts empty every
time, including when switching between profiles.

The request binds the full profile version, original draft, local chat,
loaded model and effective settings. The active model counts the
exact prompt with the chosen details and reserved reply capacity.
Generation checks those inputs and the latest stored profile before
publishing. The raw profile context is omitted from the saved
question and future prompt history. A generated reply can contain
details derived from it, and saved replies still enter ordinary
history, search, exports and chat backups. Profile storage itself
stays outside those backups. A backgrounded activity clears the
open review and unsaved profile editor.

The exact build passed 1,189 JVM cases and both lint variants with
zero errors. Each Android emulator API passed 139 cases, including
profile creation, private editing, persistence and deletion. Controller
tests verified that only the selected items reach the model, the
native preview and send receive the same prompt, and stale or
unmeasurable context cannot start a generation.

An Android 17 normal-app trial used LFM3 with networking disabled.
The reply used the selected flower note and omitted the unselected
writing preference. The original question was saved with the reply.
All 7 existing model and chat files matched their original hashes,
and the emulator network preferences were restored after the trial. The first harness attempt stopped before
profile creation because it used an incorrect caption. That attempt
also restored networking.

to Hermes automatically.

## Foreground-only temporary phone chats

Open Temporary chat from the phone Chat tab. It runs against an explicit
installed model, keeps conversation context in memory, and applies the
same exact native context budget as saved chat. A temporary request
opens no saved-chat generation record. History, search and chat backups
operate on the saved conversation store. End confirmation clears the
draft and transcript. Android stopping the activity or destroying the
process clears the temporary session. The secure dialog requests
Android screen capture protection.

Native generation releases its request context at every terminal
outcome while retaining model weights. Closing drops the in-memory
request identity before stopping active generation, so a late callback
cannot restore that transcript. These app controls do not establish
forensic erasure of Android, keyboard, runtime or system memory.

The strict build passed 1,186 JVM tests with zero lint errors. Android
17 passed all 110 focused tests. Android 8 passed 109 of 110, including
both new temporary-chat cases. The existing summary-draft viewport test
failed in the full Android 8 run. A separate run on the same build
passed that test and both temporary-chat cases. The full-run failure
remains open. The temporary-chat checks covered context and model
guards, saved draft retention, explicit close, background cleanup, and
history and search isolation.
The first stock prompt produced no usable reply and its draft remained visible.

On Android 17 the stock app used LFM3 offline for two temporary turns.
The second reply recalled the flower named in the first question. The
synthetic marker was absent from the bounded app log sample. Ending
the chat kept the model weights and reopened an empty session.
The trial preserved 7 inventoried model and chat files and restored
emulator networking.

## Reviewed offline writing tools

Writing tools accept a manually edited draft, one Android plain-text
share, or text selected in another app. Intake shows the text and
requires approval before it replaces the writing source. The source
limit is 6 KiB of UTF-8 and the editable instruction limit is 2 KiB.
Shared attachments are refused. Cancelling intake or request review keeps
the editor's draft in memory.

The review shows the loaded model and the two exact native messages.
Editing or a different model invalidates the review. Each confirmation
is consumed once, and a cancelled generation publishes no new result.
Phone chat history is separate. The five English and Chinese preset
prompts can be edited, saved as custom templates, or used for one turn.
Users can explicitly save a result in private phone writing notes.
Each library holds up to 16 saved items.

The first JVM run found that the app did not generate Kotlin serializers.
The verified writing library uses explicit, versioned JSON validation.

The strict build passed 1,183 JVM tests, both lint variants with zero
errors, and 108 focused tests on Android 8 and Android 17. A stock
Android 17 trial opened and cancelled a selected-text review before
using the real Share receiver. It selected LFM3,
reviewed the exact input, generated offline, saved a note and reopened it
after app relaunch. It removed only the synthetic test note, retained
7 inventoried model and chat files, and restored networking.

## Offline questions about PDF pages

On Android 15 and later, Documents can extract selectable text from
a chosen PDF up to 8 MiB and 64 pages, with up to 128 KiB of extracted
UTF-8 text. PDF text extraction uses Android's renderer in a non-exported
isolated service. The service receives a read-only descriptor for one
selected file. The app unlinks its empty staging file before writing bytes
and saves only the extracted pages. It can still read previous text-file
records. Password-protected and image-only PDFs show an explanation.

The review and answer cards show the original PDF page. Empty pages
preserve page numbering and excerpts stay within their page.

The initial isolated-service preflight found normal WorkManager
startup running inside the parser process. The verified app checks
Android's isolation status before ordinary application initialization
and gates the PDF API at the service entry point.

The exact debug build passed 1,179 JVM tests and 106 focused Android
tests each on Android 8 and Android 17. Both lint variants reported
zero errors. The Android tests checked the configured isolated service,
page extraction, unsupported older Android, cancellation, malformed
inputs, image-only PDFs, and both byte and page limits.

On Android 17, the stock app used the system picker with networking
disabled. It rejected a known password-protected fixture and retained
its source bytes. It indexed a separate three-page PDF, kept the blank
second page, and reopened the saved result after an app relaunch. LFM3
answered a question about the PDF and cited [S1] on page 3. The test
retained 7 inventoried model and chat files, removed its synthetic
copies, and verified that networking was restored.

## Offline questions about TXT and Markdown

On-device AI uses Android's document picker and an explicit index action.
Signal Grove stores up to 12 private UTF-8 text copies, each up to 128
KiB. A question can search up to four selected files. The review shows
at most two exact excerpts with stable citation labels, filename and
line range. The prompt carries the question and those excerpts. The
answer screen shows only outputs with usable citation markers and
displays their underlying excerpts. For a reply without markers, the
app can attach the unique source of an exact quote. Citation resolution
checks references and leaves factual verification to the reader.

Re-indexing atomically replaces the reviewed private copy. Deleting
removes only that current private record. The app never saves the
provider URI or claims directory access, and the document answer
does not create a remote request or enter normal phone chat history.
Pending question and answer content is held in memory.

The exact debug pair passed 1,178 JVM tests and 104 focused tests
per API on Android 8 and Android 17. Both lint variants reported zero
errors. Tests covered strict UTF-8, file bounds, cancellation before
publication, re-indexing, stale deletion, Unicode retrieval, isolated
scope, citation validation and the in-app review and confirmation.
The first Android 8 build rejected a Unicode regex during screen
initialization. The verified build classifies Unicode code points
without that regex.

The normal Android 17 app indexed a selected Markdown fixture through
the system picker with Wi-Fi off and no default network. After a

from the explicitly reviewed excerpt and cited [S1]. The source card

## Publisher catalogue revision updates

A fresh catalogue revision now has its own immutable HTTPS pin and
licence review. A user with an earlier model can open **Review publisher
update** from **Phone models** or **Compare downloadable models**.
The dialog shows the incoming pinned revision and hash, the earlier
installed revisions, and space needed for the remaining bytes plus
the reserve. The app keeps earlier files and conversation hashes.

The existing version 1 download receipt format is unchanged. The same
exact earlier revision can still resume when bundled as older. A
receipt for a revision unavailable in this app version stays in the
queue file with its original identity and relative order. Known items can
be added, completed or removed without erasing it. When the queue has
no space for a new entry, the attempted addition leaves the file intact.

The exact build passed 1,173 JVM tests and 103 focused methods per API
on Android 8 and Android 17. Both lint variants reported zero errors.
The catalogue-transition test used synthetic GGUF fixtures with
different pins. It verified the earlier receipt resumed under the
new catalogue, required independent approval for the replacement,
and compared both installed files and the existing chat. The Android
test verified the two visible revisions, storage summary, licence
controls and exact queue selection. Live metadata for the two
publishers still matched the shipped pins. No successor was added
to the bundled catalogue.

The Android 17 normal app acquired live Qwen publisher bytes in its
foreground service and continued after Home. The accessibility snapshot
showed the launcher and did not expose notification Pause. The harness
stopped the process and verified the retained 17,268,466-byte prefix
against the same range of the full publisher file on disk. The
existing review receipt and prefix hash matched after app relaunch.
Only an explicit resume completed publication of the 491,400,032-byte
file with the pinned SHA-256. The earlier LFM3 file matched its full
hash. The remaining inventoried model and chat files matched their
prior evidence. Inference stayed unloaded. The trial's fixture was
removed, and the emulator's notification and network settings were
restored.

A real published successor, physical-phone interruption and handoff,
low-space and reboot acceptance remain open.

## Reviewed replacement from a phone model file

picker for one installed model. After the licence review, the app stages
the picked GGUF in private storage and checks its metadata, supported
architecture, chat-template presence and tensor ranges. It displays
both SHA-256 identifiers, the new model's declared context, file size
and free space after staging. The hash identifies the file's bytes.

publishes the exact candidate as another model. Chats and performance
settings stay bound to their original SHA-256. Loading the candidate or
deleting the earlier file requires a separate action. Cancel and

replacement stages. The existing publisher-download queue keeps its

and removed its own files.

## Opt-in model downloads while away from the app

A reviewed queue item offers a separate **Download in background**
action. This starts an Android data-sync foreground service for
the exact attempt. The downloader waits for service promotion with
a visible notification. Going to Home leaves that attempt running.
An old notification cannot pause another attempt. The notification
opens the downloads list and offers Pause while safe to stop.

The action releases loaded inference weights and inherits the
saved network preference, existing partial file, full hash and
atomic publication path. Closing the ordinary download screen
keeps the original activity-scoped behavior. Notification refusal
and an expired service acknowledgement retain the item. The
service uses a non-sticky launch and its attempt identity lives
only in the current process.

The frozen build passed 1,167 JVM tests and both lint variants
with zero errors. Android 8 and Android 17 each passed 100
focused device methods. The added JVM checks cover waiting for
promotion, leaving the activity, refusing stale actions, preserving
the saved prefix and expiry without a network request. The
Android UI test and focused emulator suite verify the reviewed
entry and independent notification-settings route.

On the owned Android 8 emulator, the regular app displayed an active
model download notification. The service survived the Home button
while a loopback fixture held its one CONNECT attempt. Tapping the
notification opened the active download. The real Pause
button closed the socket. After a process restart the same reviewed
item was waiting. The test removed its own queue entry, compared
5 unchanged model and chat files, and restored the emulator proxy.
The fixture sent no model bytes.

On the owned Android 17 emulator, an 18-second test limit exercised the
system data-sync service timeout from the ordinary app. Android logged
the timeout for Signal Grove. The socket closed, the service stopped,
and there was no timeout crash. Relaunch showed the same reviewed Qwen
item with zero saved bytes and no second request. Existing model and
chat files passed retention checks. The fixture sent no model bytes.
The emulator's timeout, notification permission and network settings
were restored. Timeout log SHA-256 is ca81a3442b2dabb1fe66b14687c550b2cb9e2fabe358b6b8ffd413cd0fbc0edb.

In a second Android 17 run, revoking the temporary runtime notification
permission ended the process and closed the socket. Relaunch preserved
the exact queued item without reconnecting. This verified OS-level
revocation; stopping after a channel-only change in the same process
still needs a separate check.

Physical-phone and end-to-end publisher checks remain open. The download
notification channel also needs a visible-to-disabled trial while the
process stays alive.

## Model download network preference

The private model download client can use any network or restrict
requests to Android's current unmetered network. Any network is the
default. Unmetered only checks the default network's capabilities
before external I/O. The restricted client binds DNS and sockets
to that network and uses an isolated connection pool. If the
default network changes or loses eligibility, the callback cancels
the current call and the downloader preserves the written prefix.
The app never submits a new request from the callback. A saved file
that already has every byte can be verified offline. A preference
read failure stops the request.

The frozen build passed 1,165 JVM tests and both lint variants with
zero errors. Android 8 and Android 17 each passed 99 focused device
methods. JVM fixtures cover denied fresh and resumed requests,
invalidation followed by an explicit exact Range request, and
offline verification of a complete partial. Android tests cover
saving the choice without starting a download, the platform
classification and bound client, and a failed preference read.

The owned Android 17 emulator was checked with an explicit metered
override. Its actual default network lost the unmetered capability.
The adapter rejected that route. The original Wi-Fi metering
setting and unmetered capability were restored. The first shell and
immediate-transition observations were retained. The successful run
used the settled network state after changing the setting in Android.

## Reviewed download queue and explicit resume

A catalogue licence review can start the download immediately or
save the selected model in **Model downloads**. The private queue
persists its order and exact publisher URL, length, hash and licence
identity as a fingerprint. Adding a row contacts no publisher. Starting,
resuming and verifying saved files require a separate tap. A partial
from an older build can be reviewed without deleting its bytes.

The transfer flushes its written prefix on pause and periodically
during download. The queue shows the measured byte count and phase.
After an interruption the app reads the actual partial file length
before offering an explicit resume. The same HTTPS range validation,
full SHA-256, GGUF compatibility inspection and atomic publication
still apply. Observing an installed model removes its completed
queue receipt. An unreadable receipt preserves the installed library
and stops queue writes.

The frozen build passed 1,162 JVM tests and both lint variants with
zero errors. Android 8 and Android 17 each passed 96 focused native
methods with zero skips. The JVM cases cover ordered reread, scoped
discard, no resume without current review, corrupt-receipt retention,
and reconciliation after installation. The new device checks cover
the actual bilingual review controls, exact item/byte status, pause,
and licence review for an older partial. Android fixtures simulate
the transfer. A physical interruption and restart with this build
remain open.

The regular Android 8 app saved one reviewed LFM3 row with zero
downloaded bytes. A different app process reopened the same pin.
Removal returned the queue to empty and all 5 compared
model and chat files retained their previous bytes.

before the two action-bound assertions. The original job completed
instrumentation and retained the log and terminal record.

## Offline low-memory refusal and smaller-model recovery

The frozen copy-report debug build ran through the normal app on a
disposable API 26 x86_64 emulator configured with 2 GiB of RAM. Android
reported 2,046,976 KiB of total memory. Airplane mode was on, Wi-Fi
and the cellular data connection were off and Android reported no
default network. The emulator held two verified models and one
completed synthetic LFM3 chat.

Load model on LFM3 1.7B QAD showed the insufficient-memory error.
The displayed admission threshold was 2,258 MiB. The app had no
GGUF mappings, and the original chat matched its original hash.
After dismissing the error, the operator explicitly loaded
Qwen2.5-0.5B Instruct Q4_K_M, whose threshold was 1,194 MiB. A new
phone chat began empty. One send of `Reply with the word Grove`
completed with `Grove` in the app and in the saved chat. The saved
turn was bound to the Qwen file, which was the only mapped model.

The final check found precisely two chats. The first was byte-identical,
the second had one completed exchange, and both GGUF sizes and SHA-256
digests matched their initial values. The guest still had no default
network. Physical low-memory and sustained thermal/battery checks are
pending.

## Copy on-device performance details

Copy performance report is an explicit clipboard action for the current
model load. The report contains active numeric settings, app memory,
available timing measurements and the benchmark status. It reuses the
phone clipboard handling. Opening the panel or finishing a benchmark
leaves clipboard contents in place. The app presents Copy when
measurements or a benchmark result are available and phone work is idle.

The frozen build passes 1,157 JVM tests, both lint variants with zero
errors and 84 focused native methods on each of Android 8 and Android 17.
The bilingual test checks the clipboard payload, absence of model names
and fingerprints and absence of question and answer text. The original
Android 8 run had one fixture failure before these assertions because
the test obtained the clipboard service off the UI thread. Obtaining it
on the UI thread made the unchanged assertions pass. The original
Android 17 run passed all 84 methods. In the next Android 8 run, the
clipboard assertions passed and the protected-backup fixture scrolled
before the password keyboard had settled. The final fixture focuses the
password and waits for a coherent native keyboard viewport before
scrolling to confirmation. The original wrong-passphrase, encrypted
round-trip, immutable-source and restore assertions remain covered.

The original Android 17 inventory, before any test body ran, ended in a
process startup timeout after the APK update. A normal launch also timed
out. A reboot reached a new boot ID. Dismissing the stuck Pixel Launcher recovered normal rendering, and the
exact APK pair then passed the full test run.

## Physical LFM3 benchmark with networking off

The M098FE ran the signed debug app from the performance build above.
After the model loaded, the app reported 2,370.47 MiB of process PSS.
The phone ran the fixed prompt with a 384-token cap after the test
verified Airplane mode on, Wi-Fi and mobile data off and no default
network. The same radio and network state was verified at completion.

LFM3 reached visible text in 3.06 seconds and completed at
44.3 sampled tokens/s over 127 sampled tokens. Android reported a
29.7 °C battery sensor and thermal status 0 at both observations.
The battery was full and Android reported external power. This short
sample does not establish sustained performance or battery drain.
After the app went to the background, its process still ran and had
no GGUF mappings.

The original radio settings were restored. An initial private Pi ping
failed after Wi-Fi returned. Opening the existing Tailscale app once
restored the active tunnel and the private Pi ping. All six saved
chats, both models, labels, package UIDs and the production package
passed the post-run checks.

and passphrase state before preparing any archive. The existing review,
destination picker, encryption and restore gates remain in use.

Its [API 26 job 126207721426](https://github.com/DionCroft/Signal_Grove/actions/runs/41718591404) failed before APK installation or instrumentation: emulator **37.2.13** reported **7183 MB available / 7372.8 MB required**. No API 26 test result was produced by that job. The earlier local final suites remain 364/364/365 passing tests. API 37 from that hosted run is a separate checkpoint.

The configured 2048M preference cannot override every first-boot minimum: [Android's emulator source](https://android.googlesource.com/platform/external/qemu/+/refs/heads/emu-32-release/android-qemu2-glue/main.cpp) enforces at least 6 GiB for API 24+ and checks 1.2× capacity. The isolated prebuilt-APK device helper now checks for 8 GiB free after SDK/image installation. Only if needed, it reclaims the SDK's unused NDK installations (present on the [official Ubuntu runner image](https://github.com/actions/runner-images/blob/main/images/ubuntu/Ubuntu2404-Readme.md)); the device job never compiles native code. It validates Linux/GitHub context, the isolated temporary work root, the SDK identity and a nonsymlink direct-child NDK target before the fixed-argument cleanup, then requires sufficient space. No developer SDK, workspace, other toolchain or standing AVD is cleaned. Low capacity without that specific reclaimable tree remains an explicit failure.

ADB readiness now polls the same owned emulator process and serial under the original deadline; an exited process fails promptly with the emulator-log pointer. It does not restart on observation timeouts or rerun instrumentation. Offline regressions cover sufficient capacity/no cleanup, exact NDK-only cleanup and insufficient post-cleanup capacity, developer/wrong-root/missing-target refusal, dead-process detection, transient ADB probe timeouts on the same live process and bounded live readiness. Full hosted device validation of this helper change remains a subsequent checkpoint; no emulator was recreated or wiped on the owner's machine.
